-4-  NC: 2024:KHC-D:3781  WP No. 146992 of 2020  THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR PRELIMINARY HEARING, THIS DAY, THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 ORDER

The land bearing Sy.Nos.80/4 measuring 1 acre 16 guntas, Sy.No.81/4 measuring 1 acre 1 guntas,
Sy.No.82/3 measuring 1 acre 18 guntas and Sy.No.83/1 measuring 2 acres 36 guntas, Sy.No.83/2 measuring 12 acres 19 guntas was proposed to be acquired for the purpose of upper Krishna project which culminated in passing of an award dated 02.08.2013, and in pursuance of the award passed,
notice under Section 12(2) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (for short, 'the Act, 1894') was served on the petitioner.
The petitioner submitted the particulars for making the payment in light of the award.
However, the said application was not considered, which prompted to the petitioner to approach this Court in W.P.No.82078/2013 and connected petitions.

This Court vide order dated 04.02.2019 dismissed the petition as having become infructuous since the application submitted by the petitioner was considered and the claim of the petitioner for paying the compensation amount was rejected on the ground that the petitioner has failed to establish ownership over the subject land.
Taking exception to the same, this petition is filed.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that in the preliminary notification and final notification, the name of the petitioner was shown as owner and thereafter the award was passed the determining the market value of the acquired NC: 2024:KHC-D:3781 land.
However, respondent No.2 issued impugned endorsement stating that the company failed to prove his title over the acquired land.

He further submits that in L.A.C.No.66/2010 and connected matter, the Reference Court has held that the petitioner is not the owner of the lands, which are subject matter of the reference therein, and not subject lands, and therefore the impugned endorsement issued by respondent No.2 refusing to release the compensation is not sustainable in law.
3.

Learned Additional Government Advocate for the State submits that the petitioner having not established its title over the acquired land, the respondent No.2 has rightly refused to release the compensation in favour of the petitioner, and the same does not warrant any interference by this Court.
4. Considered the submissions made by learned counsel for the parties.

5. Admittedly, the name of the petitioner was mutated in the record of rights in respect of the subject lands and in the preliminary and final notifications, the name of the petitioner was shown in the owners column in respect of the subject lands, which culminated in passing of an award in favour of the petitioner determining the market value of the subject land.
Respondent No.2 has also issued a notice under Section 12(2) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 intimating the award passed under Section 11 of the Act, 1894.
The petitioner has produced the copy of the award passed in L.A.C.Nos.62 to 66/2010 and connected awards to substantiate that the subject lands are not the subject matter of the reference therein.
However, respondent No.2 relying on the award passed in the said cases has refused to release the compensation stating that the petitioner has not established its title over the acquired lands.

Section 12(1) of the Act, 1894 states that the award shall be filed in the collector's office and shall except as provided herein after provided be final and conclusive evidence as between the collector and the persons interested.

Therefore, the award passed is binding on respondent No.2,
and the conclusive evidence that the petitioner is the owner of the subject lands.

It is also undisputed that the claim of the petitioner is not disputed by any person and in the absence of any rival claim, the impugned endorsement issued by respondent No.2 is not sustainable in law.
Accordingly, I pass the following:

ORDER i) The petition is allowed.
ii) The impugned endorsement dated 02.08.2013 issued by respondent No.2 at Annexure-K is hereby quashed.
iii) Respondent No.2 has deposited a sum of Rs.32,81,055/- in light of the order passed by this Court on 17.07.2023.
